newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africans suspend Cuban doctor after four die.
newsitem.headline: South Africans suspend Cuban doctor after four die.

text.p: South African health officials have ordered a Cuban doctor to take stress leave after four patients died while he administered anaesthesia to them, state television reported on Friday.

Five other patients at the hospital in Pietersburg, a small town about 400 km (250 miles) north of Johannesburg, also died mysteriously over the past three months shortly after routine operations, television news said.
But hospital senior superintendent Nicholas Crisp cautioned that the issue should not be "blown out of proportion".
"It's necessary that investigations be made as with any doctor," Crisp told television.

About 450 Cuban doctors arrived in South Africa last year to work for three years in rural and township hospitals which are under severe pressure with the departure of many young South African doctors not prepared to put up with long hours, poor pay and spiralling crime.

The Cubans have been received with much scepticism in South Africa, where up to half the country's English-speaking medical graduates emigrate soon after qualifying. Only 22,000 doctors serve the population of about 43 million.
